newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight demand rises, more orders expected.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight demand rises, more orders expected.

text.p: New business picked up on the sugar freight market on Wednesday with a flurry of fresh inquiry, boosted by Middle East buying tenders and Brazil deliveries against the October raw futures contract, shipbrokers said.
"It's a bit busier -- and that's reflected in the rest of the market too," said one shipbroker.

Tunisia bought a cargo of white sugar for shipment in June 1997 after an earlier snap tender. Jordan bought 30,000 tonnes of whites in two lots for late November and first half December shipment from Louis Dreyfus.
Sri Lanka and Syria also held buying tenders on Wednesday, but the results are not expected until Thursday.
CSR issued two new bulk orders for 20/30 October, both from Queensland, the first for 30,000 tonnes to Inchon and 19,000 tonnes to Japan.

Fiji Sugar Marketing was open for 19,000 tonnes, at five percent, from Fiji to London for 1/10 November. Cargill quoted for 25,000 tonnes in bulk from Santos to Morocco with Egyptian Mediterranean and Black Sea options for 16/20 October.

E D & F Man was in the market for 25/28,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio to the Black Sea for prompt dates and a further 18,500 tonnes from Maputo to US Gulf/Atlantic for mid-October, shipbrokers said.

U.S. shippers Sugar Chartering was looking to cover 14,800/15,800 tonnes in bulk from Rosario and Montevideo to US Gulf/Atlantic for prompt dates and also 21/22,000 tonnes from the Philippines to the same destination for 20/25 October.
The only firmer reported came from Fiji Sugar Marketing, which was said to have fixed 15,500 tonnes of bulk sugar at five percent from Fiji to London at $22 for mid-October dates.
